subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How many daughter cells are produced from a single parent cell by mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis is a single division that produces two daughter cells.

questions.q: How many cells are produced from one parent cell by meiosis?
questions.explain: Meiosis involves two divisions, producing four gametes.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are found in a normal human body (diploid) cell?
questions.explain: Human diploid cells contain 46 chromosomes arranged as 23 pairs.

questions.q: How many chromosomes are present in a human gamete?
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid and contain 23 chromosomes, half the diploid number.

questions.q: The daughter cells produced by mitosis are described as being:
options: Genetically identical to the parent cell
Genetically different from the parent cell
questions.explain: Mitosis produces genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: What is an allele?
options: A different version of a gene
A section of the cell membrane
questions.explain: Alleles are alternative forms of the same gene.

questions.q: An organism that is homozygous for a characteristic has:
options: Two identical alleles for that gene
Two different alleles for that gene
questions.explain: Homozygous means both alleles for the gene are the same.

questions.q: A recessive allele is one that:
options: Is only expressed when two copies are present
questions.explain: A recessive allele is masked unless the genotype is homozygous recessive.

questions.q: In humans, which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a typical male?
questions.explain: Males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY).

questions.q: Why is mitosis, rather than meiosis, used for growth and tissue repair?
options: It produces genetically identical diploid cells
It only occurs in reproductive organs
questions.explain: Growth and repair need identical diploid cells, which mitosis provides.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the cells produced by meiosis?
options: Haploid and genetically different from each other
questions.explain: Meiosis produces four haploid gametes that are genetically varied.

questions.q: What is the difference between a diploid cell and a haploid cell?
options: A diploid cell has two sets of chromosomes; a haploid cell has one
A diploid cell has one set of chromosomes; a haploid cell has two
A diploid cell is always a gamete
A haploid cell is produced by mitosis
questions.explain: Diploid cells carry paired chromosomes, while haploid cells carry a single set.

questions.q: Why must gametes be haploid?
options: So the diploid number is restored at fertilisation
So they can divide by mitosis
questions.explain: Fusion of two haploid gametes restores the full diploid chromosome number.

questions.q: A tall plant has the genotype Tt, where T (tall) is dominant. What is its phenotype?
questions.explain: The dominant allele T is expressed even when only one copy is present.

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the observable characteristic
Genotype is the observable characteristic; phenotype is the alleles present
They both describe only recessive traits
They are two words for the same thing
questions.explain: Genotype refers to the alleles, while phenotype is the physical expression.

questions.q: An individual with the genotype Bb is best described as:
questions.explain: Two different alleles for a gene make the genotype heterozygous.

questions.q: In a genetic (Punnett) diagram, what do the letters written along the top and side represent?
options: The alleles carried by each parent's gametes
The number of chromosomes in the cell
The phenotypes of the offspring only
questions.explain: Punnett square margins show the alleles in each parent's gametes.

questions.q: Two heterozygous pea plants (Tt x Tt) are crossed, with T (tall) dominant. What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring?
questions.explain: A Tt x Tt cross gives genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, a 3:1 phenotype ratio.

questions.q: A heterozygous plant (Tt) is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant (tt), with T dominant. What is the expected phenotype ratio of the offspring?
questions.explain: A Tt x tt cross produces half Tt (tall) and half tt (short), a 1:1 ratio.

questions.q: In humans, a mother is XX and a father is XY. What is the probability that any child will be male?
questions.explain: The father's X and Y gametes give an equal 50% chance of XY (male) offspring.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Biology (2017) specification; Cell Division & Genetics
